summary: Implemented the additive Rust /server_info.kv_events discovery descriptor from typed ServerArgs, including safe JSON/TCP endpoint and port validation, null fallback behavior, and preservation of the existing allowlist/redaction boundary. Python route parity passes, but the prepared environment contains no cargo or rustc executable, so the Rust crate and its serialization tests could not be compiled or executed.

tests.command: git show 358c163250ad3b1f62939b01ce1314a0a31a0365:rust/sglang-server/src/api_server/common.rs | sed -n '/let response = serde_json::json!({/,/});/p' | grep -q '"kv_events"'
tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression: the checked-out base Rust /server_info serializer did not contain the kv_events field. Raw extracted serializer is retained in reports/j-7f9988b47f0a/rust-server-info-before.txt.

The real Python /server_info handler contract, including enabled, disabled, malformed JSON, non-TCP and malformed TCP endpoints, port bounds, page-size rejection, IPv6, and existing-field preservation: 29 tests and 12 subtests passed.
Attempted the focused Rust serialization/redaction regression suite from the prepared repository with private cache paths; the shell reported cargo: command not found before compilation.

remaining_limitations: Rust 1.92 is pinned by rust/rust-toolchain.toml, but neither cargo nor rustc is installed or discoverable in the prepared environment; therefore the Rust tests, crate build, and live Rust HTTP route remain unverified.
No GPU was used because this is an HTTP metadata serialization contract with no model-kernel execution; the frozen Torch/ROCm stack was unchanged.
KV-event publishing itself is intentionally out of scope and was not implemented or exercised.
The deterministic tiny-Llama fixture was not used because it cannot validate an uncompiled Rust metadata serializer and no model execution is involved.
